name: Host list builder
what_it_does: Creates the one inventory file every script reads: host, IP, OS, role, how to connect, scored services

name: Script test harness
what_it_does: Runs each script in dry-run and apply mode on a test VM of every target OS and reports failures. Every script goes through it as it is finished

name: Shell library (lib.sh)
what_it_does: The six jobs every Unix script repeats: argument parsing, dry-run and apply, log naming, backup with undo-log entry, protected-list check, exit codes. Also tool detection, the password generator and a quarantine function

name: PowerShell library (lib.ps1)
what_it_does: The same jobs for PowerShell 2.0, plus a CSV writer and the WMI fallbacks

name: Build step
what_it_does: Copies the library into each script so every file still runs standalone

name: Run sheet generator
what_it_does: Prints a one-page checklist per role from the host list and wave order: which scripts to run, in what order, on which hosts, with a tick box and time for each

name: Inject tracker
what_it_does: Records each inject with ID, time received, deadline, owner and status, and warns 15 and 5 minutes before a deadline

name: Config backup and diff
what_it_does: Logs in to each firewall, router and switch over SSH (Cisco IOS and ASA, Palo Alto, FortiGate, VyOS, pfSense, OPNsense, MikroTik, Linux) and saves its running config with a timestamp; drops lines that change by themselves and diffs against the last copy; changes to accounts, secrets, SNMP, NAT, permits, management services and routes are HIGH; tracks device SSH host keys; secrets masked on screen
you_give_it: Host list (or --device); SSH keys or a password in an environment variable

name: Firewall rule export
what_it_does: Turns the rule base into a CSV: number, name, source, destination, port, action, logging, hit count

name: Subnet sweep (Windows)
what_it_does: A 20-line fallback: finds live hosts with ping and arp -a when nmap isn't available

name: Network scan
what_it_does: Nmap wrapper with standard file names: fast scan, then full TCP and service versions. Falls back to a ping sweep without nmap. An "outside" profile scans the public addresses from beyond the firewall

name: Linux collector
what_it_does: One script with sections: system, listening ports, users and groups, services, scheduled jobs, SSH, packages, risky files (SUID, world-writable, immutable flags), firewall rules, config files holding credentials, containers, running processes, live connections, logged-in sessions, kernel modules, PAM settings, SELinux or AppArmor state, trust files and NFS exports. The triage profile also copies existing logs off the host. Profiles: one-page card, full inventory, incident triage

name: DNS inventory
what_it_does: Zones and records, recursion and zone-transfer settings, forwarders

name: Windows collector
what_it_does: Same design: system, listening ports, local users and groups, services and startup, scheduled tasks, software and patches, shares, firewall rules, roles, running processes, live connections, sessions, drivers, user rights and LSASS protection. Same three profiles; triage also copies the event logs off the host

name: AD user audit
what_it_does: Every domain user: enabled, last logon, password last set, never-expires, admin count, description fields holding passwords, and computer accounts with blank or default passwords

name: AD privileged groups
what_it_does: Members of Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, Schema Admins, Administrators, DNS Admins and Backup Operators, including nested groups

name: Group Policy report
what_it_does: All GPOs with links and settings; flags logon scripts and software installs

name: DNS export
what_it_does: All zones and records, forwarders and zone-transfer settings

name: Credential locator
what_it_does: Finds stored passwords the red team reads first: Group Policy Preferences in SYSVOL, unattend.xml, auto-logon registry keys, saved RDP and Credential Manager entries, PuTTY sessions, PowerShell history, logon scripts, files left on shares, connection strings in web.config

name: Service-account usage map
what_it_does: Which accounts run services, scheduled tasks and IIS app pools on every host. Run before any rotation so scored services aren't broken

name: Windows tamper scan
what_it_does: Detection only, per host. Checks the registry keys and settings the red team weakens or hides in. Common: firewall profiles off or allow-all rules, Defender off or with exclusions, UAC off, guest enabled, RDP opened, WDigest on, audit policy cleared, event log service stopped, PowerShell logging off. Less common: port forwards (netsh portproxy), added root certificates, hidden or registry-only local users, hosts file and DNS changes, proxy settings, netsh helper DLLs, LSA providers, print monitors, time providers, COM hijacks, BITS jobs, debugger keys on system tools. Writes findings with a fix ID and class for each

name: Web and database inventory
what_it_does: Linux and Unix. Web servers (Apache, nginx, lighttpd, Caddy, Tomcat, PHP-FPM) with versions and run-as accounts; every site with its port, TLS and web root; files that should not be in a web root (web shells, PHP in upload folders, database dumps, .env, .git, backups, phpinfo pages); risky php.ini settings; WordPress, Joomla, Drupal, phpMyAdmin and other apps with versions and database user; MySQL/MariaDB and PostgreSQL accounts with no password, remote root, backdoor functions, triggers and trust logins; Redis, MongoDB and similar stores open to the network
you_give_it: Nothing (extra web roots or a MySQL client file optional)

name: Web and database inventory (Windows)
what_it_does: The Windows twin of SV-01: IIS sites, bindings, physical paths and app pool accounts; the same web root file checks; MSSQL logins with empty or weak settings, sa state, xp_cmdshell, linked servers and startup procedures; MySQL or PostgreSQL on Windows

name: Linux fan-out and push
what_it_does: Fan-out means running one script on many machines at once from the admin workstation. Sets up the team automation account and key on first run, checks the kit's hash, copies the kit to every Linux host over SSH, runs a script in parallel, collects each host's output and exit code

name: Offline tool bundle
what_it_does: Gathers the standalone tools the scripts rely on (nmap, busybox, Sysinternals, Sysmon, agent installers, and audit tools such as linPEAS and winPEAS to run on your own hosts) so nothing needs internet

name: Admin workstation hardening
what_it_does: Run first, before anything else. Locks down the machine that holds the kit, credential sheet and backups: no inbound remote access, firewall to outbound only, protected folder for the kit and outputs

name: Local runner
what_it_does: The fallback when fan-out isn't working. Run by hand on one host from a USB stick, a shared folder or a pasted one-line loader. Detects the host's operating system and role, runs the same scripts in the same wave order with a pause before each stage, and saves everything to one folder to carry back to the admin workstation

name: Inventory merger
what_it_does: Combines collector and scan output from all hosts into one CSV: host, role, OS, IP, ports, services, needed or not

name: Service check library
what_it_does: One set of scored-service probes (HTTP, DNS, SMTP, POP/IMAP, SSH, FTP, SMB, RDP, database, LDAP, NTP, SNMP, VNC, Telnet, ping) with three modes: check once, watch and restart, and a live dashboard with history

name: Protected list builder
what_it_does: Reads the scoring sheet plus collector and check output and writes the protected ports, services and accounts file. Fails loudly if a scored service isn't listening anywhere

name: Allowlist builder
what_it_does: Turns user, admin, scheduled-job and startup inventory into pre-filled approved lists with suspicious entries flagged, for one human review

name: Break-glass account
what_it_does: Creates one clearly named local admin per host with a recorded password before any lockdown runs, and logs it as a change

name: Scoring traffic finder
what_it_does: Reads mail, FTP, SSH, web and database logs to find the scoring engine's source address and the accounts it logs in with, including ordinary mail users. Feeds the protected list. Reports nothing if no pattern is found

name: Credential sheet builder
what_it_does: Merges every rotation's output into one offline sheet for printing and a CSV in the scoring team's password-change format, then securely deletes the pieces

name: Device password rotation
what_it_does: Changes admin and enable passwords and SNMP communities, then confirms the new login works before closing the session

name: Password rotation
what_it_does: Sets a new random password for every account with a shell and writes the list to an operator file

name: Account lockdown
what_it_does: Locks every account not on the approved list and sets its shell to nologin

name: SSH hardening and key cleanup
what_it_does: Lists every authorized key of every account (service accounts too) and removes those not on the team's list, keeping them as evidence; puts safe settings at the top of sshd_config (no empty passwords, root by key only, no rhosts or user environment, no X11 or agent forwarding, few auth tries); tests the config with sshd -t before installing, reloads sshd and restores the old config if it stops listening; quarantines ~/.ssh/rc and /etc/ssh/sshrc; reports loosening Match blocks and key commands. Password logins stay on

name: Sudo cleanup
what_it_does: Removes NOPASSWD entries and unapproved users, including polkit rules, doas and kept environment variables such as LD_PRELOAD; validates with visudo -c before saving

name: Backup
what_it_does: Run before any change. Archives /etc, web roots, crontabs, service configs and home folders with a hash list, and sends a copy off the host. It is both the restore point if a fix breaks scoring and the baseline the change watch (LX-40) compares against

name: Logging and audit turn-on
what_it_does: auditd rules for the paths that matter, process accounting, shell history to syslog, and forwarding to the central collector

name: PAM repair
what_it_does: Reads the collector's PAM findings (permit-all lines, empty-password settings, command-running modules, replaced module files) and restores the login configuration from package defaults. Classed "may affect a service"; tests a second login before the session closes

name: Privilege escalation check (Linux)
what_it_does: Detection only. Finds the ways a low-privilege user becomes root: scripts and folders that a normal user can write to behind cron jobs, timers and sudo rules; cron commands with wildcards; writable folders on root's PATH; risky SUID and capability binaries; docker group members. Writes findings with fix IDs

name: Linux safe fixes
what_it_does: The Linux twin of WN-43: only fixes that cannot break a scored service. Kernel settings (SYN cookies, ASLR, no source routing or redirects, no IP forwarding unless the host routes), owners and modes on passwd, shadow, group, sudoers and SSH host keys, logging and auditd turned back on if stopped, an attacker-added /etc/ld.so.preload or hosts-file entry reported and reset, core dumps of setuid programs off, trust files such as .rhosts and hosts.equiv removed. IPv6 off with the kernel setting (net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6, made permanent in sysctl.d), never the ipv6.disable boot option: that one stops any service configured to listen on [::] (nginx's default does) from starting. Services listening on IPv6 are listed first. Each fix is backed up and logged for undo

name: Linux change watch
what_it_does: Light, early version of AU-13 for one Linux host. Takes a baseline, then on a timer compares: accounts, sudo rules, cron and systemd timers, SSH keys, listening ports, SUID files, PAM, ld.so.preload, files added or changed in web roots (hashes), and key config files. Each difference is written to one alerts file and copied to the admin workstation. Built on the collector (SH-05) and the scan diff (SH-04)

name: AD permissions audit
what_it_does: Finds hidden control that survives password resets: replication (DCSync) rights on normal users, full control on AdminSDHolder or an OU, odd owners on the domain object, who can edit Group Policy objects and SYSVOL scripts, unexpected rights on individual users, groups and computers, and who can read LAPS and gMSA passwords

name: AD password rotation
what_it_does: Sets a new random password on every domain user and writes the list to an operator file. Reads the usage map and refuses service and scored accounts without the extra flag

name: Account lockdown
what_it_does: Disables domain and local accounts not on the approved list and removes unapproved members from privileged groups

name: Logging turn-on
what_it_does: Advanced audit policy, command-line process logging, PowerShell script block logging; installs Sysmon if supplied

name: Backup
what_it_does: AD (system state or install-from-media copy), all GPOs, DNS zones, DHCP, IIS and service configs, with a copy off the host. Turns on the AD recycle bin on first run and can restore deleted users and OUs

name: Certificate template audit
what_it_does: If Certificate Services is installed: lists templates that let an ordinary user request a certificate as someone else, and who can enroll. Also checks the CA itself: requester-supplied names, who holds CA management rights, web enrollment over plain HTTP and unencrypted enrollment. Detection only

name: Privilege escalation check (Windows)
what_it_does: Detection only, per host. Finds the ways a low-privilege user becomes SYSTEM: service binaries, service settings and scheduled-task scripts a normal user can change; unquoted service paths with writable folders; missing DLLs in writable application folders; AlwaysInstallElevated; impersonation rights given to ordinary users. Writes findings with fix IDs

name: Windows safe fixes
what_it_does: Applies only the tamper-scan findings classed "Safe", the ones that can't break a scored service: firewall profiles on with existing allow rules kept, Defender on and exclusions removed, UAC on, guest off, WDigest off, audit policy and event logging back on, port forwards removed, hosts file reset, debugger keys and rogue helper DLLs removed. Anything that might affect a service is left for the settings baseline (WN-26)

name: Database backup
what_it_does: Dumps every MySQL/MariaDB database (one file each, including the mysql accounts database; consistent for InnoDB, with routines, triggers and events), PostgreSQL roles and databases (custom format), and SQLite files in web roots; checks each dump reads back; hashes them; restore commands per dump; can copy them off the box and keep only the newest N
you_give_it: Nothing (a MySQL client file and a destination optional)

name: Web exposure sweep
what_it_does: Detection only. Probes the team's own sites without logging in: admin pages that answer without a login, backup and config files that download, passwords in JavaScript files, plain HTTP, missing cookie flags, reflected CORS origins, open redirects on the login page

name: Persistence hunter and quarantine (Linux)
what_it_does: Checks every place malware survives a reboot: cron, systemd units and timers, rc files, shell profiles, ld.so.preload, PAM modules, MOTD scripts, udev rules. In apply mode, quarantines what isn't on the approved list

name: Persistence hunter and quarantine (Windows)
what_it_does: Run keys, services, scheduled tasks, WMI event subscriptions, startup folders, Winlogon and IFEO keys, AppInit DLLs, accessibility-tool swaps, password filters, security packages and hidden scheduled tasks. Same apply mode

name: Credential and session purge
what_it_does: For one user or everyone: ends SSH, RDP and console sessions, drops Kerberos tickets, clears cached credentials, invalidates web and CMS sessions. Run together with password rotation

name: Weakness checker
what_it_does: Detection only. Reads collector and scan output and flags known weaknesses by version and setting: SMBv1, Zerologon, PrintNightmare, HiveNightmare, unpatched EternalBlue, old sudo and polkit, anonymous FTP, TFTP, unauthenticated VNC, default SNMP community strings, default logins, Telnet, and firewall or router firmware versions from the config backups. Writes the findings file with a fix ID and class for each. Changes nothing

name: Windows fan-out and push
what_it_does: Same as AU-02 for Windows, using WinRM where it is on and falling back to WMI or PsExec

name: Backup run
what_it_does: Triggers every role's backup script, pulls the results to one protected host, verifies hashes

name: Undo walker
what_it_does: Reads a host's undo log and reverts the last change, the last N, or everything since a given time

name: Proof capture
what_it_does: Runs a named set of verification commands on a host and saves the output with host name and time, ready to paste or screenshot as inject evidence

name: Submission check
what_it_does: Before a response goes out: confirms the file name and inject ID match, searches the text for real names, passwords and unfilled [brackets], and logs the submission time

name: Tables collector
what_it_does: Interfaces, VLANs, routes, ARP and MAC tables, NAT and port forwards from each device; marks switch ports with no link as a report only

name: Device account and management audit
what_it_does: Local accounts, SNMP communities, and which management services are on (Telnet, HTTP, SSH, API)

name: Management hardening
what_it_does: SSH only, management limited to the admin subnet, idle timeout, login banner, NTP and syslog servers set, SNMPv3 in place of older versions

name: IP block list
what_it_does: Adds attacker addresses to a deny rule or address group at the perimeter, reading the shared file the hunters write to; lists and removes them too

name: Perimeter port closer
what_it_does: For each port: finds rules that allow it inbound and disables or tightens them. Refuses scored ports

name: Scan diff
what_it_does: Compares two runs of the network scan (hosts and ports that appeared or vanished, scored services that went down) or two runs of the Linux collector on one host (new accounts, SSH keys, cron entries, sudo rules, SUID files, listening ports)
you_give_it: Nothing (picks the newest two runs), or two run folders

name: Port and service closer
what_it_does: Takes ports or service names. For each: finds the service, stops and disables it, and adds a firewall block. Refuses anything protected and reports what wasn't open

name: Firewall builder
what_it_does: Drops every incoming connection except loopback, replies, ping, DHCP, SSH, scored ports (protected list), ports listening now (not backdoor-style ones) and the admin and scoring hosts; IPv6 dropped. Own nftables table or iptables chains, nothing else flushed; nft -c check; automatic rollback after 2 minutes unless confirmed from a new session; --save for reboot; optional outgoing limits and SSH source limits

name: Settings and permissions baseline
what_it_does: The settings that can affect a service, after the safe ones in LX-39: web root ownership and modes, clearing immutable flags the red team set and locking the team's own critical config files the same way, the fixes SH-14 listed for this host by class, and SELinux or AppArmor back on in permissive mode only
you_give_it: Whether the host routes; web root

name: Mail inventory
what_it_does: Domains, mailboxes, relay settings, open-relay test, TLS settings

name: File service audit
what_it_does: FTP, SMB and NFS: anonymous access, writable shares, exported paths

name: DNS hardening
what_it_does: Recursion for internal clients only, zone transfers to named servers only, version hidden

name: Local admin rotation
what_it_does: Sets a different random local Administrator password on every domain machine

name: krbtgt reset
what_it_does: Resets the krbtgt password twice with the required wait, checking replication between resets. Tested and ready by hour two

name: Port and service closer
what_it_does: Takes ports or service names. For each: finds the owning service, stops and disables it, and adds a firewall block. Refuses anything protected

name: Firewall builder
what_it_does: All profiles on, default-deny inbound, allow rules from the list (netsh fallback). Blocks all IPv6. Same "isolate" profile as Linux

name: Settings baseline
what_it_does: One settings file applied in one pass: SMBv1, LLMNR, NetBIOS and WDigest off; SMB and LDAP signing on; RDP with Network Level Authentication or off; domain password length; WinRM and PowerShell remoting limited to the admin workstation; NetNTLMv1 refused; AlwaysInstallElevated off; the WebClient service off where it isn't needed; and the registry fixes SH-14 listed for this host (Zerologon, PrintNightmare, HiveNightmare), by class. Lockout threshold stays loose so the red team can't lock scored accounts with failed logins

name: Defender check and scan
what_it_does: Turns Defender back on, removes attacker-added exclusions, updates and runs a quick scan

name: AD permissions reset
what_it_does: Removes the unapproved rights the audit found and restores default permissions on AdminSDHolder and the domain object

name: Certificate Services fix
what_it_does: If Certificate Services is installed: applies the fixes the audit listed, one at a time. Unpublishes or tightens unsafe templates, removes requester-supplied names at the CA, removes CA management rights from ordinary users, and requires encryption for enrollment. Classed "may affect a service"

name: Web application finder
what_it_does: Detects WordPress, Joomla, Drupal, Roundcube, phpMyAdmin and similar; versions, plugins, admin accounts

name: Database password rotation
what_it_does: Changes application database passwords, updates the matching app config files, then tests the site still loads

name: Database hardening
what_it_does: Removes anonymous users, remote root and test databases; on MSSQL turns off command execution, secures sa, and removes impersonation rights and linked servers mapped to sysadmin; binds to localhost unless a remote app needs it

name: Web server hardening
what_it_does: Hides versions, turns off directory listing, removes default pages, limits HTTP methods, sets security headers, disables dangerous PHP functions, turns on ModSecurity if it is already installed

name: CMS admin reset
what_it_does: Resets admin passwords, removes unknown admins, turns off the built-in file editor, fixes file permissions

name: WordPress lockdown
what_it_does: Rotates the secret keys so stolen sessions end, checks the site address setting for redirects, blocks script execution in the uploads folder, lists must-use and unknown plugins, turns off XML-RPC and open registration, and compares core, plugin and theme files with the baseline

name: Web request filter
what_it_does: Server-level rules in IIS, Apache or Nginx for flaws that can't be fixed in code quickly: limits admin paths to the admin subnet, refuses backup, database and parent-folder requests, stops script execution in upload folders, sets cookie flags and one fixed CORS origin. Classed "may affect a service"; runs the service check before and after

name: Time sync check
what_it_does: Confirms every host and device agrees on the time, so log timestamps line up

name: Change log collector
what_it_does: Gathers every host's run records and undo logs into one change log: who ran what, where and when

name: Status board
what_it_does: One screen for the captain: scored services up or down, open incidents, injects due next, and the last ten changes

name: Report generator
what_it_does: Converts script CSVs into ready-to-paste content for inject responses: asset, account, firewall and change tables, a gap table against a control checklist, and incident report fields

name: Least-privilege rule builder
what_it_does: Generates a full inbound rule set from the scored service list, with default deny and logging, and IPv6 blocked at the perimeter

name: Egress filter and outbound log
what_it_does: Limits outbound traffic from servers to what they need (DNS, NTP, updates), which breaks most reverse shells, and reports top talkers and new destinations

name: Config restore
what_it_does: Pushes a saved config back, using commit-confirm or a timed reload so a bad change undoes itself

name: Samba and NFS hardening
what_it_does: Removes guest and anonymous access, limits shares and exports to named hosts and users, turns off old protocol versions where the scoring check allows

name: Mail hardening
what_it_does: Closes open relay, requires authentication to send, disables unneeded protocols

name: FTP hardening
what_it_does: Disables anonymous login, jails users to their folders, TLS where the scoring check allows

name: Brute-force and spam banning
what_it_does: Reads SSH, FTP, mail (SMTP login, IMAP, POP), web login and RDP logs, counts failures per source address in a time window, and bans an address that passes the limit with a timed firewall rule that removes itself (nftables, iptables, ufw, firewalld or pf; fail2ban if installed). Also flags mail spam: a sender or address sending far more mail than normal, relay attempts, or a local account suddenly mailing many outside addresses. Never bans the protected list (scoring engine from SH-13, admin workstation, team subnet). Dry run lists who would be banned; every ban is logged with the evidence and shared with the perimeter block list (NW-12)

name: Bulk account changes
what_it_does: Adds and removes users with group memberships from a CSV, on Linux and in AD, with a before-and-after record

name: Share permission fixer
what_it_does: Removes Everyone and Guest access from shares and resets to the groups given

name: Kerberos exposure fix
what_it_does: Finds accounts with SPNs, accounts without pre-authentication, RC4-only accounts, every delegation type (unconstrained, constrained, resource-based) and shadow credentials; resets or fixes each

name: Group Policy restore
what_it_does: Compares live GPOs with the backup and puts a tampered one back

name: Service restore
what_it_does: Puts a web root, database, DNS zone or mail config back from the last good backup and reports what was replaced

name: Web log analyzer
what_it_does: Top source IPs, most-requested paths, and requests that look like SQL injection, path traversal or shell upload

name: Central logging setup
what_it_does: Builds a syslog collector and points Linux hosts, Windows event logs and network devices at it

name: Change watch
what_it_does: One baseline-and-compare engine for ports, users, admin groups, scheduled jobs, services, web root file hashes, config files, DNS zones, database users, the hosts file, and decoy files and accounts that nobody should touch. Also alerts when logging, antivirus or the firewall is switched off. Runs on demand or on a timer and alerts on any difference

name: Recently changed files
what_it_does: Files created or modified in the last N minutes or hours in system, web and temp paths (both platforms)

name: Log hunter (Linux)
what_it_does: Logins and failures by account and source, sudo use, new users, from auth logs and wtmp/btmp

name: Webshell scanner
what_it_does: Searches web roots for shell-like functions, odd encodings, recent dates and wrong owners, plus backdoors in .htaccess, .user.ini and PHP auto-prepend settings

name: Suspicious process finder
what_it_does: Processes running from temp or hidden paths, deleted binaries, shells spawned by web or database servers, connections to unusual ports, processes hidden from the normal listing, and connections that repeat on a timer (beaconing), with an optional short packet capture (both platforms)

name: Event log hunter (Windows)
what_it_does: Logons and failures, new users and group changes, new services, log clearing, PowerShell script blocks, Kerberos anomalies

name: Kill and quarantine
what_it_does: Records the process details and file hash, kills the process, moves the file to quarantine

name: Evidence packager
what_it_does: Copies named logs and files, hashes each, zips them, and writes a custody record with collector role and time

name: Sensitive data search
what_it_does: Searches home folders, shares, web roots and database dumps for Social Security numbers, card numbers and similar patterns, and lists file, line count and owner without printing the data itself (both platforms)

name: Job installer
what_it_does: Installs the service watch and change watch as cron jobs or scheduled tasks on the right hosts, and removes them

name: Network map data
what_it_does: Joins ARP, MAC and scan data into one table of host, IP, MAC, switch port and VLAN

name: Diagram renderer
what_it_does: Turns the map data into a Graphviz or diagrams.net file, so the network diagram isn't drawn by hand

name: Switch protections
what_it_does: If a managed switch is present: reports, then applies per port, port security, DHCP snooping, ARP inspection and BPDU guard. Never touches ports marked as uplinks

name: Inject tool installer
what_it_does: If the installers are in the offline bundle: stands up the tools injects commonly ask for (LibreNMS, Nagios or Zabbix monitoring; IPv6 addressing on hosts) with safe defaults and a change record

name: Hardening menu
what_it_does: An interactive menu that calls the scripts above one at a time and records what ran. No logic of its own

name: Container hardening
what_it_does: If Docker or Kubernetes is present: lists privileged containers, exposed sockets and mounted docker.sock, and fixes what it safely can

name: LDAP directory password rotation
what_it_does: If a Linux directory server (OpenLDAP, FreeIPA) is present: rotates directory user passwords with the same refusal rules and output file as local rotation

name: Hardening menu
what_it_does: An interactive menu that calls the scripts above one at a time and records what ran

name: Service provisioning
what_it_does: Adds a website, share or DNS record on request, opens exactly the one firewall rule it needs, and writes the change record

name: Certificate check
what_it_does: Every TLS certificate in use: expiry, issuer, key size, self-signed or not

name: Certificate maker
what_it_does: Creates a self-signed or internal-CA certificate and installs it on the web or mail server

name: Appliance and admin console finder
what_it_does: If present: finds Splunk, Webmin, phpMyAdmin, Jenkins, Tomcat manager, Roundcube, e-commerce admin panels, firewall web consoles and similar; reports version, who can reach it, and whether a known default login still works. Exits quietly if none are found

name: Appliance and admin console lockdown
what_it_does: If present: rotates the admin password on each console found, removes unknown admin users, and limits the console to the admin subnet. Skips anything it doesn't recognize

name: Data store lockdown
what_it_does: If Redis, MongoDB or Elasticsearch is present: requires a password and binds it to localhost or the named app hosts

name: Security tool deployer
what_it_does: If the installers are in the offline bundle: installs and configures a log or detection agent (Wazuh, Splunk forwarder, Sysmon, ClamAV) on each host and points it at the collector. Does nothing if the installer isn't there

name: Practice planter
what_it_does: For practice only: plants harmless red-team-style changes on a test VM (extra admin user, cron job, SSH key, startup entry, open port, web file) so the team can check the hunters find them. Refuses to run on any host not on the test list, and removes everything it planted

name: Binary integrity check
what_it_does: Verifies system files against the package database (rpm -V, debsums) or sfc

name: Indicator sweep
what_it_does: Searches every host for given IPs, file names, hashes, account names or strings

name: Timeline merge
what_it_does: Joins the CSV output of the hunters from several hosts and sorts by time. Nothing more

name: First-15-minutes run
what_it_does: One command that runs collectors, backups, rotation and purge in the agreed order across all hosts, with a checkpoint after each stage

name: Restore run
what_it_does: Restores one host's configs or data from the central backup, with a preview of what will be overwritten

name: Hypervisor inventory and snapshot
what_it_does: If the team can reach a hypervisor (ESXi, Proxmox, Hyper-V): lists VMs, networks, users and management services, and takes a snapshot of each VM before hardening starts

name: Hypervisor hardening
what_it_does: If present: rotates the hypervisor admin password, turns off its shell and SSH when not needed, removes unknown users, and limits management to the admin subnet
